parsed.explanation: Combined federal and state regimes impose state-enforced birth-sex facility exclusion in airports and other public buildings, with criminal/civil penalties and private bounty suits, plus birth-sex passport rules, document-discrepancy refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility, and documented birth-sex custody harm including forced labour and sexual abuse. Functioning courts, anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, and injunctions on some orders provide partial recourse, but courts have also allowed passport restrictions and the bounty mechanism needs no prosecutor. No documented execution or likely long imprisonment for presence alone. This is a Tier-1 universal exposure well below protective jurisdictions.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passport sex is birth-sex binary; X/non-matching markers stopped, Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025. Cable directs refusal on document discrepancy and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility. Passports confiscated/blocked, travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; ACLU suit for seven plaintiffs and challenges unresolved; some federal orders enjoined. No documented visitor-specific exemption.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger refusal, investigation and fraud allegation, concentrating border, detention and placement risks in one encounter.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Arrest example: handcuffed, held 24 hours in men's ward, trespass charge. Federal corrections model reports hair cutting, hormone removal, conversion therapy; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime and employment law exist; courts sometimes enjoin orders. No documented birth-sex-custody safeguard or effective remedy for custody abuse in dossier.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility or document enforcement can lead to detention where birth-sex placement and documented abuse become operative, regardless of state anti-discrimination law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars government-funded facilities congruent with identity. Division law effective Feb 2026 confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in publicly owned buildings including airports, schools, universities and offices, up to $1,000 penalties.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State has prohibited gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations since 2020, but dossier does not show it overriding the specific facility ban. Some bans are government-only; 29 states have no mapped ban, but this division does.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Anyone using a public building, including an airport transit, faces the same birth-sex rule; private bounty suits do not require a prosecutor.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders target gender-affirming care for minors and public funding; state bans care for minors under 18. Hospital ward placement by birth-sex documents is part of federal facility regime. Customs/medication seizure not documented.
care_services.protection: Not documented for adult visitors seeking hormone continuity. Emergency-care protection not documented.
care_services.interaction: School, hospital and government-facility rules converge on birth-sex documents; a minor visitor also faces state care prohibition and school facility exclusion.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Bounty-style suits of at least $1,000 by any private person claiming to have shared a bathroom with a trans person; ID invalidation notices; federal guidance links radical gender ideology to extremism and prioritises pro-transgender groups in counterterrorism strategy.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009; state hate-crime law does not. Legal challenges and advocacy are active, and several orders are blocked/enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Private enforcement plus official threat-framing increases reporting, confrontation and police-call risk beyond formal prosecution.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division schools are covered by birth-sex facility ban; under-18 gender-affirming care banned in state and 27 states nationally. Federal order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition, including names/pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: May 2026 temporary injunction blocked enforcement in one parental lawsuit; municipal conversion-therapy bans exist but are resident-facing, not visitor protections.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces school/public-building facility exclusion and guardians may face investigation or care-access barriers; adult guardian cannot cure birth-sex document rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Legal-risk assessment moved division to Do Not Travel citing bounty law; plaintiffs cite fear of violence. No sourced count of visitor assaults, bounty suits filed, or enforcement frequency in dossier.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; state public-accommodations law since 2020. Whether prosecutors use national law for state-excluded offences is not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Social hostility and bounty incentives can produce confrontation or police involvement even where no trans-specific assault pattern is quantified.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: 2023 TRO reversed, Oct 2025 highest court allowed ID changes; passport suit unresolved; bounty enforcement data and licence-notice numbers not recorded. Remedies are slow, costly and uncertain for short visitors.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined some federal orders; civil-liberties organisations represent plaintiffs; legal-aid FAQ exists. No documented remedy that reliably reverses facility exclusion or bounty suit before departure.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Efficient courts enforcing hostile passport/facility rules are exposure, not mitigation; litigation may help residents long-term but does not protect a visitor during travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal stops, fines and ineffective complaints, but this case is lower: documented birth-sex custody sexual abuse, permanent fraud-ineligibility risk at entry, and private bounty enforcement add severity beyond hours-long detention with rare imprisonment.

Similar birth-sex confinement, short penalties and no execution, with assault risk in men's facilities. This case is higher because functioning courts have enjoined some orders, state anti-discrimination law since 2020 and national hate-crime coverage exist, and long imprisonment is not documented as likely.

Unlike 0.65-A where national equality law overrides local mismatch and compensation follows briefly, here the restrictive federal and state rules are operative, courts allowed passport restrictions, and no reliable visitor remedy for facility exclusion is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: birth-sex passports and entry screening can cause refusal or fraud exposure; birth-sex facility law in airports and public buildings carries fines and private bounty suits; any detention risks birth-sex custody with documented abuse and hormone removal. State anti-discrimination law, national hate-crime coverage, legal aid and occasional injunctions are real protections but do not override the specific facility, document or custody rules, and courts have upheld key restrictions. Minors face additional school-facility and care bans. Hence high risk, mitigated from severe-risk by functioning courts and absence of likely imprisonment or execution for presence.
